public_rationale: Cursor's completed acquisition challenges the assertion that AI investments have no exit route. It does not establish the proceeds received by particular VC holders or settle whether a substantial collection of other holdings will eventually collapse. The forecast has no deadline, defined investment population or measurable collapse threshold. The available records do not settle the complete proposition.
limitations: Under the ordinary corporate-finance meaning of acquisition as a liquidity event, the no-liquidity component faces direct counterevidence.
No financial verdict is available with the stated unknown valuation basis.
Unresolved does not mean that the no-exit explanation is supported.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: VC holdings in AI companies will eventually crater or go to zero because no liquidity events will occur.

statement.excerpt: This means that venture capitalists that have sunk money into AI stocks are going to be sitting on a bunch of assets under management (AUM) — the same assets they collect fees on — that will eventually crater or go to zero, because there will be no way for any liquidity event to occur.

from_speaker: venture capitalists that have sunk money into AI stocks
a bunch of assets under management
will eventually crater or go to zero
there will be no way for any liquidity event to occur
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns losses on VC holdings in AI startups, not merely whether an AI company raises financing.
Crater means a severe loss of investment value. No percentage threshold, investment cohort or deadline is supplied.
A completed acquisition challenges the asserted absence of exit routes. Establishing realized liquidity for VC holders requires evidence about their consideration, sale restrictions or proceeds.
A single successful exit does not settle whether an unspecified substantial collection of other holdings will eventually collapse.
criteria.support_condition: Identifiable VC-held AI investments suffer severe, durable write-downs or write-offs without realizable exits, with evidence that unavailable liquidity caused the losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented realized exits for the relevant VC holdings contradict the no-liquidity component. Resolving the broader collapse forecast also requires a defined investment population and loss criterion.
